questions.q: A teacher tells the technician that the learner's behavior plan does not work in class. What should the technician do?
options: Pass the concern to the supervisor promptly
Change the plan to fit the classroom
Tell the teacher the plan is correct
Ignore it because the teacher is not the supervisor
questions.explain: Concerns and suggestions from caregivers, teachers and other providers go to the supervisor without delay. The supervisor decides whether the plan changes. Changing it alone, or dismissing the concern, would step outside the technician's role.

questions.q: A parent suggests a new reinforcer that the learner loves at home. What is the best response?
options: Start using it right away in every program
Thank the parent and share the idea with the supervisor
Tell the parent only the supervisor may talk about reinforcers
Write it down and keep it for the next renewal
questions.explain: Caregiver input is valuable, and the technician's job is to relay it promptly. The supervisor may add the item to a preference assessment or to the plan. Using it before the supervisor agrees could change the program without review.

questions.q: A speech therapist recommends a different way to prompt words. How should this be handled?
options: Use both prompting methods at once to see which works best
Stop all prompting until the team meets
Report the recommendation to the supervisor for coordination
Ask the parent which method to use
questions.explain: Coordinating with other providers is the supervisor's responsibility. The technician reports the recommendation promptly and keeps following the current plan until the supervisor gives direction.

questions.q: A technician is unsure how to run a new program the supervisor wrote. What should they do?
options: Run it the way a previous client's program worked
Skip the program until the next visit
Look for instructions on social media
Ask the supervisor for direction before running it
questions.explain: Technicians seek clinical direction when they are unsure about a procedure. Guessing can harm the learner and makes data meaningless. Skipping programs without telling the supervisor also changes treatment.

questions.q: A technician notices that the data show a sudden drop in a skill that had been mastered. What is the right step?
options: Tell the supervisor about the irregularity promptly
Delete the low data points so the graph shows the real level
Go back to teaching it as a new skill
Wait to see whether it improves next month
questions.explain: Data irregularities are reported to the supervisor in a timely manner, who decides what to do. Deleting data is falsification, and changing the program on one's own steps outside the role.

questions.q: A technician has a concern about a procedure and the supervisor is not reachable. What should they do?
options: Decide alone and explain later
Use the organization's chain of command to reach another supervisor
Post the question in an online forum
Ask the learner's family to decide
questions.explain: Organizations set a chain of command for when the supervisor is unavailable. Following it gets clinical direction from a qualified person. Online forums break confidentiality, and families do not supervise treatment.

questions.q: A learner arrives very sleepy, and the caregiver mentions a new medication. What should the technician do?
options: Give advice about the medication
Change the reinforcers for the day
Note it objectively and report it to the supervisor
Leave it out because it is medical
questions.explain: Illness, medication and sleep can affect behavior and progress. The technician reports the facts promptly without giving medical opinions. The supervisor decides whether anything in the plan should change.

questions.q: The learner's school schedule changed this week. Why should the technician report it?
options: Only so the technician can change their own working hours
Because the BACB records schedules
So the learner can skip sessions
Schedule changes can affect behavior and progress
questions.explain: Changes in routine, such as a new school schedule, can explain changes in behavior and in data. Reporting them in time helps the supervisor interpret the graphs correctly.

questions.q: A learner's family is moving next month. What is the technician's best action?
options: Inform the supervisor so continuity of services can be planned
Stop collecting data until the move is over and services restart
Tell the learner sessions are ending
Start new goals to finish before the move
questions.explain: Life events like a move can affect progress and services. The supervisor and organization plan for transitions. The technician reports, keeps implementing the plan, and does not change goals or announce endings alone.

questions.q: During a session, the learner refuses all food and seems in pain. What should the technician do?
options: Diagnose the cause
Follow the workplace health procedure and inform those required
Continue the session as usual without telling anyone
Offer the learner medicine from home
questions.explain: Health concerns are reported following workplace procedures and the law. The technician does not diagnose or give medication, and continuing as if nothing happened could put the learner at risk.

questions.q: Which sentence belongs in an objective session note?
options: The learner was in a terrible mood today
The learner cried because he hates me
The learner cried for 3 minutes after the tablet was removed
The session went fine
questions.explain: Objective notes describe observable events, measures and context, such as a duration and what happened before. Opinions, guesses about feelings or motives, and vague statements cannot be checked and are less useful to the supervisor.

questions.q: When should session notes be completed?
options: Whenever the technician has some free time later in the week
Only when a session went badly
Once a year for the renewal
When the workplace and funders require
questions.explain: Session notes follow legal, regulatory and workplace requirements, including timing and format, which funders often specify. Late or missing notes can affect billing and the continuity of care.

questions.q: A technician made an error in a signed session note. What is the right way to correct it?
options: Use the workplace's dated correction procedure
Erase the note and write a new one with the right details
Leave it because it is signed
Ask a coworker to change it
questions.explain: Records are corrected through the employer's procedure, usually a dated amendment that keeps the original visible. Erasing or rewriting records hides changes and can be seen as falsification.

questions.q: A caregiver asks what happened during the session. What should the technician share?
options: Their own opinion of the treatment plan and the goals chosen
An objective summary, within what is allowed
Details about other clients
Advice on changing the plan
questions.explain: Technicians can describe what occurred objectively, within the limits set by the supervisor and the workplace. Opinions on the plan and plan changes are the supervisor's domain, and other clients' information is confidential.

questions.q: A technician writes the note at the end of a session. Which entry would the supervisor accept as objective?
options: The learner was in a bad mood all afternoon
The learner seemed lazy during table work
The learner cried for 4 minutes after the tablet was removed
The learner was manipulative with the parent
questions.explain: An objective entry describes what was seen and measured: the behavior, its length and what happened just before it. Words like bad mood, lazy or manipulative are interpretations of inner states or intent, which another observer could not check and which can be unfair to the learner and family.

questions.q: During a home session, the technician notices a new large bruise on a learner's arm. What should they do?
options: Tell the supervisor now and follow the reporting rules
Ask a sibling what happened and keep it quiet
Wait to see if more bruises appear next week
Photograph it on a personal phone for coworkers
questions.explain: Possible signs of harm are reported at once to the supervisor and handled under the employer's policy and the reporting laws that apply. Asking siblings, waiting or sharing photos from a personal phone delays help and breaks confidentiality. The note records only what was observed.

questions.q: A parent asks the technician to start a new toilet training program the parent read about online. What is the best response?
options: Start it today since the parent requested it
Refuse and say the plan can never change
Pass the request on to the supervisor
Try it for a week and report the results
questions.explain: The technician implements the plan the supervisor wrote and passes caregiver requests to that supervisor, who decides whether and how to add a program. Starting or trialing a program alone goes beyond the role, and refusing outright ignores a reasonable family request.
